s1.syndrome_frame: Painless testicular swelling with associated epididymal involvement and adrenal gland abnormalities
salient_findings: Enlargement and inhomogeneity of the right testis and epididymis
key_facts: 82-year-old man
Painless right testicular swelling of several weeks’ duration
History of glaucoma, prostatic adenomectomy, and hernioplasty
Medications: dorzolamide, lansoprazole, and dutasteride
Testicular ultrasound showed enlargement and inhomogeneity of the right testis and epididymis
Ipsilateral hydrocele
No systemic symptoms
Normal electrolytes, blood count, iron studies, protein electrophoresis, glucose, renal and liver function, thyroid profile, LDH, and β2-microglobulin
Negative serologies for active HCV and EBV
Positive for past EBV
No asthenia, headaches, abdominal pain, striae, or “buffalo hump”
Blood pressure was 130/80 mmHg without hypertensive peaks on 24-hour monitoring

Metastatic disease to the adrenal glands

shortlist.label: Testicular lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Painless testicular swelling and epididymal involvement with intense uptake on PET/CT

shortlist.label: Leydig cell tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Testicular ultrasound showed enlargement and inhomogeneity of the right testis and epididymis

shortlist.label: Seminoma
shortlist.why_kept: Painless testicular swelling and associated epididymal involvement

shortlist.label: Primary adrenal lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral macronodular adrenal enlargement with homogeneous attenuation on CT scan

shortlist.label: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Intense uptake on PET/CT and lack of systemic symptoms

raw.rationale: The patient's age, painless testicular swelling, and ultrasound findings are consistent with testicular lymphoma, which is a common testicular cancer in older men. The intense uptake on 18 FDG PET/CT in the right testis further supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Leydig cell tumor
rejected.why: Leydig cell tumors are typically associated with hormonal symptoms, which are absent in this patient.

rejected.label: Seminoma
rejected.why: Seminoma is more common in younger men and often presents with testicular pain.

rejected.label: Primary adrenal lymphoma
rejected.why: The adrenal nodules showed no uptake on 18 FDG PET/CT, making primary adrenal lymphoma less likely.

rejected.label: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: While this is a type of lymphoma, the presentation and imaging findings are more specific for testicular lymphoma.
